---
title: "Penguin Morphology in Three Principal Components"
format: html
---

## Learning goal

Use the direction of the first three principal-component scores to explain how one penguin differs from another across bill, flipper, and body-mass measurements.

## Why a 3D view?

A two-dimensional PCA view omits the third component. This lesson asks whether inspecting PC3 changes the interpretation of observations that appear close in PC1 and PC2.

```{r}
#| label: build-penguin-scene
#| echo: true
source("../../R/utils.R")
source("../../R/zzz.R")
source("../../R/render_scene.R")

metrics <- c("bill_length_mm", "bill_depth_mm", "flipper_length_mm", "body_mass_g")
penguins <- palmerpenguins::penguins[, c("species", metrics)]
penguins <- penguins[complete.cases(penguins), ]
row.names(penguins) <- NULL

set.seed(2026)
selected <- unlist(lapply(split(seq_len(nrow(penguins)), penguins$species), function(index) {
  index[unique(round(seq(1, length(index), length.out = 8)))]
}), use.names = FALSE)
lesson_penguins <- penguins[selected, ]

pca <- prcomp(lesson_penguins[, metrics], center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
scores <- pca$x[, 1:3, drop = FALSE]
scene_data <- data.frame(
  x = scores[, 1] / max(abs(scores)),
  y = scores[, 2] / max(abs(scores)),
  z = scores[, 3] / max(abs(scores)),
  label = paste(lesson_penguins$species, seq_len(nrow(lesson_penguins)))
)

render_scene(
  scene_data,
  x = "x", y = "y", z = "z",
  labels = scene_data$label,
  output_dir = "scene",
  title = "Penguin morphology PCA data space"
)

round(summary(pca)$importance[2, 1:3], 3)
```

[Open the interactive PCA lesson](scene/index.html)

## Interpretation prompt

Choose one penguin, cite at least one PC coordinate, and explain how its direction differs from another observation. Then check whether PC3 changes a conclusion based on PC1 and PC2 alone.

## Reproducibility

The source data come from the CC0-licensed `palmerpenguins` package. Selection and PCA are deterministic, the browser scene is generated from the saved coordinates, and `rlearnxr::check_lesson()` records project checks and an artifact hash.
